criteria.reasoning: Non-alnum ASCII sets a pending separator, emitted as one hyphen only between alphanumerics. Gives 'hello-world'.
NFKD plus skipping combining marks yields creme-brulee-a-la-carte.
Non-ASCII chars with no decomposition are silently skipped. The space after them provides the separator, so the result is 'tokyo-2026'.
Empty input leaves output empty, so ValueError is raised.
No alphanumerics are emitted, so ValueError is raised.
The default of 50 truncates 80 'a' characters to exactly 50.

test_adequacy.reason: Checks the exact 50-character length. It does not exercise the default together with hyphens, but that matches the scenario.
Covers 0 only. Negative values hit the same `< 1` check.

findings.title: Dropped non-ASCII characters do not act as separators
findings.detail: slugify('a東b') returns 'ab', not 'a-b'. The spec says dropped characters are removed, so this is defensible. 'Every run of non-alphanumeric characters becomes a hyphen' could be read the other way, and no scenario covers it.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify in the spec whether untransliterable characters between letters join the neighbouring letters or act as a separator.

riskiest_assumptions: Untransliterable characters are meant to be dropped without acting as separators, so 'a東b' gives 'ab'.
str.isascii() combined with isalnum() matches exactly [A-Za-z0-9], with no surprises from compatibility characters after NFKD.
The harness's passing tests are the real run of the committed code, and no hidden tests cover edge cases such as a negative max_length or a truncation that falls exactly on a hyphen.
